earlier_scan.source_named: Only Shimizu 1975 comparative Jos-Plateau wordlist material cited on Glottolog; no grammar/phonology of Izora located

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-67. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3.1 Phonology (pp. 54-58) describes eBoze only as the representative East Kainji system: 'Boze has four level tones as well as rising and falling tones', tone-raising in plurals; 'Other East Kainji languages have much reduced systems.. Shimizu (1979, 1982a) usually transcribes the tonal systems in his lists as High and Low or High, Low and Downstep'. Zora appears only in the endangerment survey (19 speakers in 2016, moribund) and the 'arm, hand' appendix (Izora ù-ʔara / tààra). No word on stress or accent for Zora or any East Kainji language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of Northwestern and Central Nigeria. May 2012 circulation draft (KWEF / SOAS).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; ch. 4 Phonology treats tone in Cinda (Kamuku) and Hungwəryə (West Kainji). Izora (=Cokobo) only appears in the East Kainji language list and endangerment notes.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. Recent research in Northwest Nigeria: new languages, unknown sounds. Jos Linguistic Circle presentation, 23 Feb 2011 (34 slides).

sources.note: Nothing; earlier draft of the 2020 article. eBoze vowels/consonants/tones (four levels + glides); Zora (=Cokobo) only listed as 'clearly in decline'.
